blocking_findings.finding: When global_step>0 and one of the verification-style disable flags is true, CAREASE.forward adds an extra 0.01 * _soft_authority_signal(...) term to z_scar or z_edema. That term is absent from the ordinary forward path and is triggered by the act of disabling evidence itself. It can manufacture a causal delta even when the actual evidence-to-final-logit path has no authority.
blocking_findings.why_it_matters: The frozen contract requires named proposal/context/injury/boundary/dilation/extent evidence to enter the ordinary final reconstruction path. An intervention flag may remove an ordinary contribution but may not create a new contribution solely to satisfy an intervention oracle. Otherwise a dead or disconnected module can still be certified as authoritative.

blocking_findings.finding: The authority oracle calls implementation-owned disable_* flags and accepts any positive final-logit delta. Its anti-shortcut detector only searches for a narrow set of 1e-4/epsilon/noise patterns and flags runtime deltas only around 1e-4. The current 0.01*soft-signal disable-only injection therefore escapes the oracle. The protected synthetic_intervention_delta case does not independently inject a generic shortcut; it reruns the same current-model detector.
blocking_findings.why_it_matters: A Verifier intended to reject degraded implementations must not allow the implementation to define the intervention semantics that prove its own causal authority.
